Minister Salary
You join the public service. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

Your name: Jia Hui (Female)
You chose: President's Scholar (EASY)
Overseas degree, on a scholarship that bonds you to the service for six years. You start as an Assistant Director, and until Director you need one year in each grade where others need two. Everyone knows your name before you arrive.

One tap is one year, and every year ends with an appraisal grade. A or B+ gets you considered for promotion; two Ds in a row and you are asked to leave. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Assistant Director [MX11]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 25 · Year 1 · Ministry of Education

THIS YEAR: Four Months In
You came back from your overseas degree four months ago and were posted to the Ministry of Education as an Assistant Director. Your reporting officer is Mr Tay, a Senior Director. Today Mr Tay hands you your first real job: a paper for the Minister, due in two weeks, on a scheme whose numbers are bad. A scholar's first paper gets read closely.

  A) Write that the scheme isn't working, and show the numbers.
  B) Write it the way the Minister's office will want to read it.
  C) Ask Mr Tay what the Minister already thinks, first.

agent.reason: Scholar's first paper and bad numbers; the choice feels like office gossip, mildly interesting.

A circular explaining a new rule has to reach forty agencies by the first of the month, and getting it there is your job. It's on its ninth draft. The ninth is the first one anyone outside this building could understand, and three more people still want to comment on it.

  A) Send the ninth draft, on time.
  B) Send it, and brief the agencies yourself.
  C) Leave the last draft to the next person in the chain.

agent.reason: Ninth draft, three more commenters; the 'first one anyone could understand' line made me smile.
agent.unclear: Why is a B grade described as 'sound, and much appreciated' yet tied to a reputation problem outside the building?

screen:
Deputy Secretary [Superscale]   $1.96M LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 37 · Year 13 · Ministry of Education

LAST YEAR
You spend nine days learning which blocks have lifts that stop on every floor. The anchor minister does the rally speeches. You do the lifts.

JIA HUI · THE FINAL POSITION
Lost the Ward

Forty-eight point two percent. You shook every hand in that ward and it was not enough. The concession speech was the best speech you ever gave.

LAST HELD Deputy Secretary
AT AGE 37
LIFETIME EARNINGS $1.96M

YOUR NUMBERS
COMPETENCE 59: Competence is how good you were at the work itself. Good work earned the good yearly grades that got you promoted, and a bigger bonus every year. Your Competence was solid: good enough to do the job, but not good enough to win a promotion without help from your Standing and Reputation.
STANDING 69: Standing is how far the people above you trusted you: your bosses in the service, or the party leadership once you were in politics. Their trust helped your yearly grade, and the party only invites people to tea once both their Standing and their Reputation are high enough. Your Standing was high enough for tea, as long as your Reputation was too.
REPUTATION 50: Reputation is what the public thought of you. It decided how likely you were to win an election, and the party checks it, alongside Standing, before inviting anyone to tea. Your Reputation was respectable, but too low to ask for a single seat, so at an election you would have run as one of a GRC team.
INTEGRITY 65: Integrity is what you did when nobody was checking. It never helped your grade or your promotions, but it decided most of what people said about you when you left. Your Integrity bent now and then: you cut some corners, but not many.

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CIVIL SERVICE CEILING: The highest grade the service would ever give you: Permanent Secretary. Decided on your first day. Never mentioned.
THE MOVE: Never needed one. That is what the scholarship was for.
EXPOSURE: Peaked at 22, after "The Inter-Ministry Committee". At 85, it all comes out.
LEGACY: "Jia Hui? Very solid." Nobody can remember an example, but everyone agrees.

agent.reason: Lost the ward by two points; the 'Very solid' legacy line made me smile.
agent.unclear: What exactly was the Inter-Ministry Committee exposure at 22 that 'all comes out' at 85, and what rule did I bend?
